strings.name: Andrew Wiles
strings.role: Number theorist · Proved Fermat's Last Theorem
strings.summary: Andrew Wiles connected elliptic curves, modular forms and Galois representations, proving Fermat's Last Theorem through modularity of semistable elliptic curves. His 1993 announcement contained a gap, repaired in collaboration with Richard Taylor before publication in1995. He also advanced Iwasawa theory with Barry Mazur and others. The2016Abel Prize recognized both the proof and the new directions its methods opened in number theory.
strings.coverageNote: Research checked through 13 November 2026; selected milestones extend to 2026. This is not a daily news archive. Shared achievements are credited to collaborators and teams.
strings.influence.rationale: Proved Fermat's Last Theorem and advanced elliptic-curve research, profoundly influencing modern number theory and public awareness of mathematics.

strings.highlights.highlight-1.title: Fermat's Last Theorem
strings.highlights.highlight-1.text: Solved the centuries-old integer-equation problem through modularity of semistable elliptic curves.
strings.highlights.highlight-2.title: Methods in modern number theory
strings.highlights.highlight-2.text: With collaborators advanced Iwasawa theory and Galois representations, connecting different areas of number theory.
strings.timeline.event-1.title: Regius-chair succession announced
strings.timeline.event-1.text: The UK government announced James Maynard as his successor to Oxford's Regius mathematics chair.
strings.timeline.event-2.title: Oxford Regius professorship
strings.timeline.event-2.text: Became the first holder of Oxford's newly established Regius mathematics chair.
strings.timeline.event-3.title: Copley Medal
strings.timeline.event-3.text: The Royal Society recognized his contributions to number theory.
strings.timeline.event-4.title: Abel Prize
strings.timeline.event-4.text: Recognized for the proof of Fermat's Last Theorem and the number-theory methods it opened.
strings.timeline.event-5.title: Complete proof published
strings.timeline.event-5.text: His paper and the companion paper with Taylor appeared in the Annals of Mathematics.
strings.timeline.event-6.title: Repaired the proof with Taylor
strings.timeline.event-6.text: Worked with Richard Taylor after a gap was found, completing the crucial repair.
strings.timeline.event-7.title: Announced the argument
strings.timeline.event-7.text: Presented his argument at a Cambridge lecture before detailed scrutiny.
strings.timeline.event-8.title: Iwasawa main-conjecture work
strings.timeline.event-8.text: Proved a major Iwasawa-theory result with Barry Mazur, developing methods for later number-theory research.
strings.timeline.event-9.title: Princeton professorship
strings.timeline.event-9.text: Joined Princeton as a mathematics professor, continuing work on elliptic curves and modular forms.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Cambridge doctorate
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Completed doctoral research under John Coates on reciprocity laws and the Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture.
strings.timeline.event-11.title: Oxford mathematics degree
strings.timeline.event-11.text: Completed undergraduate mathematics at Merton College before graduate study at Clare College, Cambridge.
strings.timeline.event-12.title: Born in Cambridge
strings.timeline.event-12.text: Born in Cambridge, England; encountered Fermat's Last Theorem in a library as a child.
